With known $V\succ0$ and full-column-rank $X$, define GLS $\hat\beta=(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}X^TV^{-1}Y$, prove it is BLUE by whitening, and state $\operatorname{Cov}(\hat\beta)=(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}$. For known $\beta,G,R$ under joint Gaussianity, state $E[b\mid Y]=GZ^TV^{-1}(Y-X\beta)$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(b\mid Y)=G-GZ^TV^{-1}ZG$. For unknown fixed effects, define $\hat b=GZ^TV^{-1}(Y-X\hat\beta_{\rm GLS})$ as the BLUP and give $\operatorname{Cov}(b-\hat b)=G-GZ^TV^{-1}ZG+GZ^TV^{-1}X(X^TV^{-1}X)^{-1}X^TV^{-1}ZG$; distinguish this known-$V$ result from empirical BLUP with estimated variance components. independent_mathematical_checks.dimension_defect: If a row basis K is (n-p)×n, K^T is n×(n-p), so K^T times n-vector Y is undefined for p>0. The corrected K is n×(n-p), making K^T Y an (n-p)-vector.
independent_mathematical_checks.annihilation: X^T K=0 implies K^T X=0. This is the same error-contrast condition as row-basis Krow X=0 after transpose.
independent_mathematical_checks.boundary: At p=n with full rank X, col(X)^perp={0}. There are no nonzero contrast coordinates; the empty-vector law carries no covariance information. This does not remove the p=n LMM/GLS/BLUP branches.
independent_mathematical_checks.singular_latent_covariance: No inverse of G is introduced. Gaussian contrast law allows singular V; the density/REML likelihood specifically assumes V positive definite.
independent_mathematical_checks.basis_invariance: Fixed Kprime=K A entails S_theta_prime=A^T S_theta A; determinant factor (det A)^2 and identical quadratic form give a positive parameter-free likelihood factor.
